name: 114. Bedrock Nova multimodal embeddings - taskType envelope, modality labels, detailLevel (nova-embeddings)
description:
Pins `amazon.nova-2-multimodal-embeddings-v1:0`, the third Bedrock embedding family after Titan and Cohere. It shares nothing with either on the wire:

```
{"taskType": "SINGLE_EMBEDDING",
 "singleEmbeddingParams": {"embeddingPurpose": "GENERIC_INDEX", "embeddingDimension": 3072,
                           "text": {"truncationMode": "END", "value": "..."}}}
```

AWS requires `embeddingPurpose`, `text.truncationMode` and `video.embeddingMode` while defaulting none of them, and rejects unknown keys at every level of the body - so unlike Titan and Cohere, nothing here can be forwarded blind and every required field must be supplied by the converter. 114.A1 and 114.B1 reaching 200 is what proves that.

`singleEmbeddingParams` is a oneOf over `text`/`image`/`audio`/`video`: one modality per request, no `document` at all, and no batch on InvokeModel (`SEGMENTED_EMBEDDING` is StartAsyncInvoke-only). Both limits are refused locally rather than forwarded, because AWS reports a second modality key as `required key [video] not found` - naming a key the caller never wrote - and a dropped second input would return one correct-looking vector for a two-input request. 114.A7 and 114.A8.

Nova labels every vector with the modality that produced it, and `AUDIO_VIDEO_SEPARATE` is the only place in the embeddings API where one input returns two vectors of different modalities - 114.A9. Token counts arrive only in `X-Amzn-Bedrock-Input-Token-Count` (0 for every media modality), so 114.A1 doubles as a check that the header backfill covers this family and 114.A3 that media bills nothing.

`detailLevel` (`STANDARD_IMAGE` / `DOCUMENT_IMAGE`) is optional with a valid default, so a 200 cannot tell forwarding from dropping: 114.A5 sends an invalid value and requires AWS to reject it, which only happens if the key was on the wire. It is the one field here found by reading the AWS reference rather than by probing, since AWS reports unknown keys but never optional ones.

Nova has no encoding options at all, so `encoding_format: base64` is served by encoding the float vector locally - the openai-python default path (114.A6, the Nova twin of 53.E3).

Not covered here: `SEGMENTED_EMBEDDING` via StartAsyncInvoke, which is unimplemented; audio-only input, whose label is already pinned by the audio half of 114.A9; and `s3://` sources, which Nova resolves itself but which would tie these rows to a bucket only one account has. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/embeddings-schema.html. Run with FEATURE=nova-embeddings.

item.name: 114.A1 bedrock/amazon.nova-2-multimodal-embeddings-v1:0 - SINGLE_EMBEDDING text returns a 3072-dim vector labelled text

exec: var body = pm.response.text() || '';
pm.test('Nova text embedding succeeds', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'failed: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(200);
var j; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {
pm.expect.fail('response was not JSON: ' + body.slice(0, 300)); return; }
var data = j.data || [];
pm.test('one vector, 3072 dims by default, modality text', function () {
pm.expect(data.length, 'wrong vector count; body: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(1);
pm.expect(Array.isArray(data[0].embedding), 'embedding is not an array').to.be.true;
pm.expect(data[0].embedding.length, 'Nova defaults to embeddingDimension 3072').to.eql(3072);
pm.expect(data[0].modality, 'Nova labels every vector with its embeddingType').to.eql('text');
// Nova reports token counts ONLY in X-Amzn-Bedrock-Input-Token-Count; its body has none. A zero
// or missing prompt_tokens here means the header backfill stopped firing for this family.
pm.test('usage is backfilled from the Bedrock token-count header', function () {
pm.expect(j.usage, 'no usage block: the response-header backfill did not run').to.be.an('object');
pm.expect(j.usage.prompt_tokens, 'prompt_tokens missing or zero').to.be.above(0);

item.name: 114.A5 [EXPECT-4XX] bedrock/amazon.nova-2-multimodal-embeddings-v1:0 - an invalid detailLevel is refused by AWS, proving the key is forwarded

exec: // The only way to tell "forwarded" from "silently dropped" for an optional field whose default is
// also valid: if detailLevel never reached AWS this request would return 200 with STANDARD_IMAGE.
// A 400 naming detailLevel proves it did. Bifrost does not police the enum - AWS's list is AWS's to keep.
var body = pm.response.text() || '';
pm.test('AWS rejects the value, so the key was on the wire', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'expected 400; a 200 means detailLevel was dropped before the AWS call: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(400);
pm.test('the error names detailLevel', function () {
pm.expect(body.toLowerCase(), 'error does not mention the field: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.include('detaillevel');

item.name: 114.A6 bedrock/amazon.nova-2-multimodal-embeddings-v1:0 - encoding_format base64 is encoded from the float vector

exec: // THIS IS THE openai-python DEFAULT PATH: the SDK sets encoding_format=base64 itself whenever the
// caller does not name one, so this row stands in for every plain embeddings.create() against Nova.
// Nova has no encoding options at all - no embedding_types, no embeddingTypes - so base64 can only be
// served by encoding the float vector locally, the same path Titan and Cohere v3 take (53.E3).
var body = pm.response.text() || '';
pm.test('encoding_format base64 succeeds on a model with no encoding options', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'failed: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(200);
var j; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {
pm.expect.fail('response was not JSON: ' + body.slice(0, 300)); return; }
var data = j.data || [];
pm.test('embedding is a base64 string, labelled base64', function () {
pm.expect(data.length, 'no embedding returned: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(1);
pm.expect(data[0].embedding, 'expected a base64 string; a float array means the request was downgraded').to.be.a('string');
pm.expect(data[0].encoding_format, 'representation label missing').to.eql('base64');
pm.test('the string decodes to a 3072-value float32 vector', function () {
var b64 = data[0].embedding;
pm.expect(b64, 'not base64 charset').to.match(/^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$/);
pm.expect(b64.length % 4, 'not a whole base64 quantum').to.eql(0);
var bytes = (b64.length / 4) * 3 - pad;
pm.expect(bytes % 4, 'byte length is not a multiple of 4, so it is not float32 data').to.eql(0);
pm.expect(bytes / 4, 'wrong dimensionality for Nova at its default width').to.eql(3072);

item.name: 114.A8 [EXPECT-4XX] bedrock/amazon.nova-2-multimodal-embeddings-v1:0 - text and image in one entry is refused as a modality clash

exec: // singleEmbeddingParams is a oneOf over text/image/audio/video, so Nova cannot embed a text and an
// image together the way Titan multimodal and Cohere v4 can. AWS does report this, but as
// "required key [video] not found" - a message naming a key the caller never wrote. Bifrost refuses

var body = pm.response.text() || '';

pm.expect(body, 'unexpected error text: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.include('one modality per request');
pm.expect(body, "leaked AWS's confusing oneOf message").to.not.include('required key [video]');
